title.narrative: Cabo Delgado Joint Response

description.narrative: The JR proposes a multi-sectoral response to the IDP crisis in Cabo Delgado, in line with the HRP 2021 which puts forward this approach (see UN Sector Analysis). SOS will implement in Cabo Delgado, and will prioritise the following districts: Mecufi and Metuge. SOS CV works to ensure 5,000 people are able to meet their basic food needs (FSC-I2) through food packages distributions to Households in line with cluster recommendations. SOS CV will reach 17,550 individuals and will mainstream protection throughout the response in line with HRP objectives, and also ensures specific programming to ensure people receive an appropriate response to protection risks (PRO-I2), are provided with information (PRO-I5), are reached by the implementation of specific GBV prevention measures (PRO-I11), UASC are specifically supported to address their various and complex needs (PRO-I8), and children receive support specific to their needs (PRO-I15). This includes: - Unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) services including identification and case management, linkages with agencies for Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) and provision of family-based alternative care, including support to informal foster families. - Establish community protection committees at shelter centres to support and promote a community-based approach to protect women, men, girls and boys from different background. This includes training to members of community protection committees, local leaders and Internal displaced people in GBV, PSS incident reporting mechanisms. - Training of teachers in CP and provision of PSS and disability inclusion - Capacity building of CFS facilitators and PSS animators on Child Protection, psychosocial support, including PFA, Child Safeguarding, PSEA & GBV.
